whatTheyArgued: Thymic selection as I could confirm it (reviews known by title/abstract only; full text not read). Developing T cells (thymocytes), each with a randomly generated antigen receptor, are tested on self-peptide/MHC in the thymus. Positive selection keeps cells able to recognise self-MHC; negative selection removes strongly self-reactive cells (Klein, Kyewski, Allen and Hogquist 2014 summary as found; Reza and Ritter 1998 title and topics). Selection is a two-sided affinity test that most cells fail, which I take from the field's standard account but could not confirm in text I fetched.

scholarship.ref: L. Klein, B. Kyewski, P. M. Allen, K. A. Hogquist, 'Positive and negative selection of the T cell repertoire: what thymocytes see (and don't see)', Nature Reviews Immunology (2014) (listing and summary seen; full text paywalled and not read)
scholarship.supports: selection by receptor interaction with self-peptide/MHC; deletion of autoreactive cells (negative selection) and MHC restriction (positive selection) shape the repertoire
scholarship.disputes: I did not read the article, so I cannot report its disputes. Note the URL listed in search results (nri1085) may be a different Nature Reviews Immunology item; verify the citation before relying on it.

ourUse: kernel/witness.js: a candidate is admitted as an Observation only with evidence anchored to the encounter; otherwise refused with a reason ('no evidence', 'anchor mismatch'). Handle comment: 'nomination is not admission'. Note also the thymus entry in the compendium: 'nominated for the repertoire... must survive the selection test before it is licensed'.

bends.ours: A candidate is 'nominated' and then 'licensed' by selection.
bends.theirs: Thymocytes are not nominated; receptors arise by random rearrangement and cells are tested. 'Nomination' is our word and 'licensed' is our gate vocabulary.

bends.ours: Admission = explicit evidence whose anchor matches the encounter (a presence-and-match test).
bends.theirs: Selection tests receptor affinity for self-ligands: positive selection needs enough recognition of self-MHC, negative selection removes excess self-reactivity. It is a window on affinity, not a check that evidence is attached.
Two opposed tests (positive and negative selection) at different stages and sites; the code has no analogue of negative selection (removing candidates that are too self-matching).
Correct: nothing to credit; the manifest is copyrighted_deferred and says Miller and Burnet are not quoted. The analogy is ours.
